source_read: PDF, online-first version (PDFs/MDMA/Barnett_2020_RetractionCaseStudy.pdf): publisher cover page, then article pp. 1-7, all read; p. 5 rendered at 110 dpi to count the Discussion's paragraphs; Table 1 (50 newspapers) and Table 2 (17 reporting components) checked row by row, and eight of the Fisher's exact p values recomputed from the counts. The 2021 issue pagination (pp. 104-110) was not checked.

design.note: Cross-sectional is right: a one-time census of coverage in 50 newspapers, with proportions as the main outcome. 'Survey' would also fit and takes the same instrument; nothing turns on the choice.

instrument.note: JBI prevalence checklist, which scripts/rob_vocab.py allows for a cross-sectional design, and the vocabulary used (yes, partial-yes, no, not-applicable; overall low/moderate/high as the editors' summary) is within METHODS §5.3.

key_findings.note: p. 2, Introduction, 6th and 7th paragraphs: the Gazette announcement, the AAAS release and its closing line, the New York Times sentence, the MAPS criticism and the authors' defence citing a novel protocol.

p. 2, Introduction, 9th and 10th paragraphs: no NIDA report, the January 2004 FOIA release indicating a further retraction, Blakemore's call for an independent inquiry, the Nature editorial on coverage and the Illicit Drug Anti-Proliferation Act, and the Spain trial.
p. 3, Results, 1st paragraph; every count and both p values as printed.
p. 3, Results, 2nd paragraph; all four means, SDs and ranges as printed. I repeated the editors' recombination check: 483 and 396.

p. 3 Results, 3rd paragraph and Table 2 (p. 4). Every count and percentage in the card matches the table. I recomputed eight Fisher's exact p values from the counts (0.61, 0.35, 0.16, 0.06, 0.61, 1.00, 0.55, 0.61) and they agree with the printed values.
p. 5, Discussion, 5th paragraph (the paragraph that begins 'Among the entire sample'), checked on the rendered page.

p. 5, Discussion, 6th paragraph. The note is right and important: the Parrott (2013) cited there is Human Psychopharmacology 28:289-307, a different paper from the review carded in this batch, and Doblin et al. (2014) is the only source given for the regulatory sentence.
p. 5, Discussion, 4th paragraph for the late-Friday quotation from the Nature editorial and 7th for the three limitations.

reporting_issues.note: 'two of them died' (p. 2) against the 2003 reply's 'one of ten monkeys' (Mithoefer et al., p. 1504).
14 of 20 is 70% by my calculation, and that figure appears nowhere in the paper; the abstract and the Discussion both lead with the conditioned 54%.

The reference list (pp. 6-7) prints Parrott (2011) as Addiction 106(7):1365-1268 and Fisk et al. (2011) as 106(7):1268-69; the PDF of the Parrott letter runs pp. 1365-1368 with the Fisk letter starting on p. 1368.

domains.note: partial-yes: a 2007 ranking used for 2002-2003 coverage, and replacement of newspapers without archives.
14 of the top 64 skipped, which I confirmed from the Methods ('descend the list of largest newspapers to number 64 in rank').
My Wilson intervals for the three headline proportions are 38.5-65.2%, 27.6-53.8% and 35.5-71.2%, so about 14 points either way is right.
'no' is right: no coding scheme, coder, blinding or reliability, and 'balanced' is never defined.

'no' is right: the paired publication-versus-retraction comparison and the word-count difference are untested. My own exact McNemar test on the 12 and 6 discordant newspapers gives p=0.24, and a Welch test on the word counts p=0.25, so the untested comparisons would not have been significant either.

overall.note: Moderate is defensible: the coverage counts are simple and reproducible in principle, while the two 'no' items fall on the content analysis and the untested comparisons. The card's reasoning already limits what may be cited to the counts, which is the right consequence, and JBI has no overall algorithm (METHODS §5.3), so the 'never less severe than the worst domain' rule does not force high here.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. 'Moderate' and 'concerning' in the abstract rest on 26 against 20 of 50 newspapers with no test, and the explanations offered in the Discussion (press release, parkinsonism angle, media narrative, late-Friday release) are untested in this design.

missed: The paper gives no date on which the archives were searched, and no second searcher or verification of the searches. Since the counts are the only part of this study the encyclopedia means to cite, the missing search date belongs on the card (it bears on JBI item 6 and on reproducibility).

The Introduction (pp. 1-2) states that the publication 'may have influenced the passage of anti-drug legislation targeting recreational MDMA use and slowed efforts to gain FDA approval', sourced to MAPS documents and a Nature editorial, and the Discussion returns to it. The card records the Discussion's version in the interpretation gap but not that the same claim frames the study's rationale, which is the clearest place where the second author's role enters the design.

The abstract's sentence that retraction stories 'were balanced, but shorter than those on the article's publication' states the word-count difference as a finding although it is untested; the card notes the absence of a test in the analysis field, but the abstract wording is itself part of the interpretation gap.
